Built for every human on earth — not just the already-connected

NOVA is the first AI platform designed from day one to serve every human on earth — the CEO in New York, the student in Chennai, the farmer in rural Kenya, the grandmother in São Paulo. It is not a chatbot, not a workflow tool, and not a developer kit. It is a complete AI-powered life operating system available on any device, in any language, with or without internet.

No polished consumer AI app works fully offline today. All require constant internet. NOVA works identically online and offline.

NOVA runs a compressed Llama 3 model on-device, paired with local Whisper STT and local TTS. On a $20 Android phone with 4GB RAM, the full AI pipeline runs without any internet connection. When connectivity returns, NOVA syncs memory, logs, and queued actions transparently.
Local LLM: Llama 3 8B quantized (Q4) — 4.5 GB, runs on 4GB RAM devices
Local STT: Whisper small model — 150MB, works offline in 50 languages
Local TTS: Kokoro open-source TTS — natural voice, 80MB, 20 languages
Sync engine: queues all actions taken offline, replays and syncs when online
Bandwidth mode: 2G-optimized UI, compresses all cloud API payloads by 80%
End-to-end voice in 95 languages on a personal installable app does not exist anywhere in 2026.

3.5 The Intent Extraction Prompt — The Platform's Brain
This is the exact Claude system prompt that enables natural speech without user prompts:
You are NOVA's intent engine. Users speak naturally — never in structured prompts.
Extract intent and return ONLY valid JSON. No explanation. No markdown fences.
"goal": "one sentence — what the user wants to achieve",
"entities": { "time": null, "person": null, "location": null, "topic": null, "amount": null, "language": null },
"spoken_response": "Warm, natural 1-2 sentence reply to speak aloud",
Rules: Always extract intent. Never refuse. Steps must be 2–4 human-readable actions.

NOVA is not just an AI platform — it is a fully agentic coding assistant. When you describe a software requirement by voice, upload a requirements document, or explain a feature in plain language, NOVA autonomously plans, writes, executes, and validates the code on your behalf. No IDE required. No manual prompting. No context-switching. Just speak, approve the plan, and ship.
9.1 How It Works — The Agentic Coding Loop
The agentic coding pipeline runs as a single continuous loop from requirement to running code, without manual intervention between steps:
You speak your requirement, upload a specification document, or paste a user story. NOVA accepts all three with no reformatting required.
The intent engine extracts the coding goal, target language, framework, files to create or modify, and any constraints (performance, accessibility, security).

NOVA generates a numbered development plan in plain English: which files to create, which functions to write, which dependencies to install, and which tests to run. Shown as an approval card before any code is written.
You say “yes do it” or tap Approve. You can edit any individual step, skip a step, or cancel the entire plan before a single line of code is written.

NOVA writes every file to your local filesystem via Computer Use mode, installs dependencies, runs the code in a sandboxed terminal, and captures output. All steps are streamed live so you see exactly what is happening.
NOVA runs automated tests, checks for errors, and self-corrects. If a test fails, NOVA diagnoses the issue, proposes a fix, and asks for approval before applying it.
NOVA speaks a summary of what was built, the files created, tests passed, and any next steps. The session is saved to memory so you can resume or extend the work in any future session.
NOVA accepts coding requirements in three ways, all feeding the same agentic pipeline:

Speak your requirement naturally in any of 95 languages. Example: “Build me a REST API in Node.js with Express that has user authentication using JWT and a PostgreSQL database.” NOVA transcribes, extracts intent, and begins planning immediately.

Upload a product specification, PRD, user story, or technical brief (PDF, DOCX, or plain text). NOVA reads the full document, extracts all coding tasks, maps them to the build phases defined in the document, and creates a sequenced development plan. A complete product spec like this one becomes a full automated build roadmap.

After seeing the initial plan, say “add rate limiting to the API” or “use TypeScript instead of JavaScript.” NOVA revises the plan in real time. The full conversation is stored in memory so every refinement builds on the last.

9.4 From This Spec to Running Code
Upload this specification document to NOVA and say: “Build NOVA.” NOVA will read the full spec, map every section to a build phase, and present the following automated development plan:
Scaffold the Node.js + FastAPI backend, set up PostgreSQL with pgvector, create the intent extraction API, and build the plan-before-act engine.
Build the React frontend with VoiceButton, plan cards, and module panels. Wire to the backend API. Package as Electron desktop app.
Implement the pgvector memory store, fact extraction pipeline, and context injection. Test persistence across sessions.

Each phase executed in sequence, with approval before each phase begins. All 16 modules, 7 background agents, offline mode, React Native mobile app, and 20-language support built autonomously per the roadmap in Section 6.

Every phase requires your approval before execution begins. You can pause, redirect, or extend the plan at any point. NOVA remembers the full build history across sessions — you are never starting from scratch.
